claims.claim: Project hooks are configured in .cursor/hooks.json with "version": 1; user hooks in ~/.cursor/hooks.json.
claims.evidence: Page lists project-level <project-root>/.cursor/hooks.json and user-level ~/.cursor/hooks.json, and states both require a "version": 1 field. It also lists Enterprise and Team locations with priority Enterprise → Team → Project → User.

claims.claim: Supported events include preToolUse, beforeReadFile, beforeShellExecution, beforeMCPExecution, subagentStart, sessionStart, preCompact.
claims.evidence: All seven names appear in the page's agent-hooks event list, alongside others (postToolUse, postToolUseFailure, subagentStop, afterShellExecution, afterMCPExecution, afterFileEdit, beforeSubmitPrompt, stop, afterAgentResponse, afterAgentThought, sessionEnd, plus tab hooks beforeTabFileRead/afterTabFileEdit and workspaceOpen).

claims.claim: Hook entries support command, timeout, matcher, and failClosed.
claims.evidence: Per-script fields listed: command (required), type ("command" default or "prompt"), timeout (seconds), loop_limit, failClosed (boolean, default false), matcher (regex; empty or "*" matches all).
claims.quote: when true, hook failures block the action

claims.claim: The permission/deny output shape for beforeShellExecution and preToolUse is JSON on stdout with permission: allow|deny and optional user_message/agent_message.
claims.evidence: Both schemas use permission plus optional user_message and agent_message, but beforeShellExecution's permission is allow|deny|ask (not just allow|deny), and preToolUse additionally accepts an optional updated_input field; the page notes "ask" is accepted in schema but not enforced for preToolUse. Exit code 2 also blocks; other non-zero codes fail open.

other_relevant_facts: Additional config locations: Enterprise hooks at /Library/Application Support/Cursor/hooks.json (macOS), /etc/cursor/hooks.json (Linux/WSL), C:\ProgramData\Cursor\hooks.json (Windows); Team hooks are cloud-distributed via dashboard (Enterprise only). Priority: Enterprise → Team → Project → User.
Project-level hooks run from the project root; user-level hooks run from ~/.cursor/.
Hook entries support type: "prompt" (LLM-evaluated) in addition to the default "command".
loop_limit field applies to stop/subagentStop hooks (default 5, null = no limit).
Exit code semantics: 0 = success, 2 = block action, other codes = fail-open (allow by default) unless failClosed is true.
preToolUse can return updated_input to modify the tool input.
Event list also includes beforeSubmitPrompt, afterAgentResponse, afterAgentThought, sessionEnd, stop, tab hooks (beforeTabFileRead, afterTabFileEdit) and workspaceOpen.

Subagents inherit all tools from the parent, including MCP tools from configured servers; cloud subagents instead use MCP servers configured at cursor.com/agents.

Token diagnostics: each subagent has its own context window and consumes tokens independently; running five subagents in parallel uses roughly five times the tokens. Trade-offs cited: startup overhead and higher token use during parallel runs; benefits: context isolation and specialized focus.
Three built-in subagents: explore (codebase search), bash (shell commands), browser (browser automation); they handle context-heavy operations automatically to keep the main context small.

Invocation: the agent proactively delegates based on task complexity/scope, custom subagent descriptions, and current context; users can request a specific subagent with /name syntax or by mentioning it naturally.
Guidance: for simple single-purpose tasks (e.g. generate a changelog, format imports) use a skill or command instead of a subagent; avoid creating dozens of generic subagents.
